messages.content: 尋找兩家電影院，位於聖地牙哥附近，提供下午5點的《天能》和晚上7點半的《007生死交戰》場次。

function.name: find_movie_showing
function.description: Find local movie theatres and their schedule for a specific movie Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. San Diego, CA

message.reasoning:
The user wants two theaters near San Diego offering showtimes at specified times for movies Tenet (which is actually called 天能) and No Time To Die (007生死交戰). We need to use the tool find_movie_showing with location=San Diego, CA? They said "nearby". We'll just set location="San Diego, CA". Provide time array ["17:00", "19:30"] maybe.

We also have to specify movie param as either "Tenet" or "No Time To Die"? But they want both. So we might call twice? Or provide an array of movies? The schema says movie can only be one value from union type. It doesn't allow multiple values. That means we can't pass both. Maybe we should do separate calls per movie/time combination. However the requirement: "Find two cinemas ... providing afternoon 5pm showing of Tenet and evening 7:30 pm showing of No Time To Die." This implies each cinema has those showings. So we could search for each movie separately but combine results manually. Let's attempt to get list of theaters that match each criteria individually then cross-match them.

But the tool expects single movie input; so we will first query for Tenet at 17:00, then for No Time To Die at 19:30. Then filter intersection of theater names.

Let's proceed:

First call: location="San Diego, CA"; movie="Tenet"; time=["17:00"]

Second call: location="San Diego, CA"; movie="No Time To Die"; time=["19:30"]

We'll produce output accordingly.
